citation.description: _fetch_ref now detects a failed fetch, checks _remote_ref_absent, and calls _delete_local_ref when the remote is reachable and the ref is provably absent — pruning the orphan so read() returns None (free).

criteria.criterion: After a remote holder acquires, a local pass reads, and the remote holder releases, a later local read(..., remote="origin") reports the lock FREE (not HELD).

citation.description: release() calls _delete_local_ref(repo_root, ref) unconditionally when remote is not None, clearing the local half after the remote CAS delete.

criteria.criterion: release(..., remote="origin") leaves no local refs/reconciler/lock behind.

citation.description: test_orphan_local_ref_is_reclaimable drives the full sequence and asserts reads_free or stolen is not None; test_preexisting_orphan_is_pruned_on_read covers the production shape where the remote releases on another runner.

criteria.criterion: A stranded local ref is reclaimable without manual intervention — either it reads free, or steal() breaks it.

citation.description: _remote_ref_absent returns False (not absent) when ls-remote exits 0 (ref present), and None (unknown/fail-closed) on transport errors — so a live remote lock is never treated as free. test_a_genuinely_held_remote_lock_is_still_respected (test_lock_orphan_local_ref.py:188) guards this.

criteria.criterion: A GENUINELY live remote holder still reads as HELD, so cross-machine mutual exclusion is preserved.

citation.description: The fix is entirely within _ref_lock.py's _fetch_ref and release functions — no new local pass source, scheduler, hook, or bridge entry point is introduced. The module docstring confirms the remote-authoritative design.

criteria.criterion: No local pass source is introduced or required: the Reconciler Bridge runs on GitHub Actions only.
